# Adaptive definition fixtures

These canonical JSON examples exercise the Aquarium definition interfaces.
Native/source hashes in bindings are placeholders. No example is an admitted
bundle or evidence of native validity, graph qualification or agent execution.

| Fixture | Definition result | Remaining claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| documentation.binding.json | Format-positive documentation-only producer, assessment and outcome mapping | Full native graph, due-capability derivation and qualification are not established |
| performance.binding.json | Format-positive baseline/change measurements with a separate comparison Decision | Full native graph and measurement semantics are not established |
| documentation.fragment.json | Format-positive ordinary work fragment with explicit evidence and assessor ports | A representative flattened native instance is required before reuse |

Unit mutations reject unknown runtime/self-identity fields, unsupported versions,
invalid family callers, unknown local references and parent-goal assessment inside
ordinary fragments. Signature controls cover every current canonical Judge and
upstream-quality operation, typed aliases and extra harmless records. They reject
Worker-only evidence, text verdicts and pass-only assessment applicability, while
preserving unrelated pass-only checks. Unknown signatures and mandatory count
maxima without an exact criterion-capacity proof return not-established. Valid
capacity bounds retain compatibility. Approval, provenance declaration, port and
closeout-reference mutations provide focused negative controls.
Native-invalid and whole-graph incompatible cases belong to the later native and
structural qualification layers; definition rejection does not relabel them.
